name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for two weeks first. This gives us real-world data on its impact without risking disruption. The trade-off is delayed immediate gains, but we avoid breaking builds or slowing teams while proving value. After two weeks, we’ll have hard numbers to decide whether to expand or drop it.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode won’t catch PR-Agent’s worst flaw: false negatives. It won’t flag reviews it *should* have made but missed, so we’d still ship broken code while patting ourselves on the back for "safe testing." Instead, run a parallel PR-Agent instance on a *subset* of low-risk PRs for a week—compare its output to human reviews, then measure both false positives *and* false negatives before trusting it anywhere. The deciding metric: error rate parity with human reviewers within two weeks.
